title: Can a Dying Star Glow Without Telling Its Story?

segments.text: Can a dying star glow without telling its story?
In the 1970s Stephen Hawking proved black holes emit faint Hawking radiation.
The glow’s temperature comes solely from the black hole’s mass, so the spectrum depends only on mass, electric charge, and spin.
Identical black holes therefore emit identical thermal radiation, a random soup of particles.
The final burst reveals only those three numbers, not whether the star was a red giant or a neutron star.
Hawking argued the pure quantum state becomes a mixed state of radiation, conflicting with quantum‑mechanical unitarity.
The radiation thus hides the original story

question: Which would you expect to survive the final burst, information or mystery?
